extracted.intended_audience: legislators, administrators, policymakers, and legal professionals concerned with unemployment insurance administration and administrative procedure
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and improvement of the administrative procedure governing individual unemployment insurance benefit decisions (from application to final, unappealable decision), including decision-making, information, appeals, enforcement, and safeguards. Focused on federal Unemployment Insurance Commission practice and law in Canada.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of the administrative process
rubrics_metrics.description: the initiation of the administrative process
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers the moment the procedure is launched by a member of the public or a public authority and includes completion of application forms, data checks, opening the file and other first-stage formalities (see Chapter 1: The preliminaries; Section 3: Initiation of the procedure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of information essential to the decision
rubrics_metrics.description: the collection of information essential to the decision
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes thorough compilation and presentation of facts prior to decision-making (gathering the facts, benefit control, fact-finding by appeal tribunals). Includes use of Record of Employment, submissions, and reports of proceedings as documentary sources for decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation in the development of the decision
rubrics_metrics.description: public participation in the development of the decision
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes opportunities for claimants and third parties to participate before decisions are taken (information sessions, clarification by agents, chance to present evidence), and the right to be heard both before and after the decision (Section on claimant participation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Machinery for consultation, notice, or prior amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: the machinery for consultation, notice, or prior amendment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers formal processes for consultation and prior notice when rules or procedures change. Includes requirements for informing the public and affected parties about procedural or substantive changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: the updating of decisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures and mechanisms for reviewing and updating administrative decisions over time, including linkage of benefit periods to labour market conditions and rules for adjusting entitlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avenues of recourse (internal and external)
rubrics_metrics.description: the avenues of recourse, whether to the originator of the decision or to a higher authority
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encompasses internal review, appeals to Boards of referees, appeals to the Umpire, and review by the Federal Court; includes filing procedures, notice of appeal, submissions, leave to appeal, and remedies available in Federal Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machinery for monitoring subsequent to decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: the machinery for monitoring subsequent to decisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes benefit control programmes, initiation and conduct of investigations, reporting, and ongoing monitoring to ensure decisions are implemented and any overpayments or abuses are detected and acted upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties applicable for failure to carry out the decision
rubrics_metrics.description: the penalties applicable for failure to carry out the decision
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers both administrative penalties and criminal sanctions: their basis and nature, imposition and recovery, the delineation between types, and procedural safeguards (e.g., warning claimants of sanctions, restricting criminal liability to provisions of the Act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities and time-frames for each stage of the process
rubrics_metrics.description: the formalities and time-frames for each stage of the process
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses filing deadlines, time required to draft and forward appeals, limitation periods (e.g., sec. 49(4)), processing times at Boards and Umpire, and organizational measures (computerization, integration) to speed decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of sources and internal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: internal rules, manuals and practices as sources of administrative procedure and their (lack of) public accessibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes three levels of sources—legislation/regulations, internal rules (minutes, policy statements, circulars, guidelines, manuals), and administrative practices—and argues for greater openness and publication of internal procedural rules to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equilibrium between administrative effectiveness and protection of individual rights
rubrics_metrics.description: balance between effectiveness of administrative action and protection of the rights of the public
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative effectiveness requires accurate information, speed in decision-making, and guarantees that decisions will be carried out; protection of rights requires prior knowledge of legal situation, opportunities to participate, and avenues of recourse. The report uses this equilibrium as a core evaluative principle for procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informing the public: general information (pamphlets, audio-visual)
rubrics_metrics.description: informing the public about the scheme using pamphlets and audio-visual methods
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to improve pamphlets, use audio-visual methods, address non-official languages, and more generally the 'duty to inform' so insured persons and employers understand entitlements and obligations (Chapter 9: Informing the public).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to legal information: text of the Act, regulations, rules of procedure, and caselaw
rubrics_metrics.description: access to the legal rules: the text of the Act and Regulations, rules of procedure, and caselaw
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for easier public access to legislation, regulations, procedural rules and relevant caselaw; notes special problems where procedural rules are internal and not published (Chapter 9, Section 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Individualized information and claimant understanding of process
rubrics_metrics.description: individual information: understanding the process via information sessions, explanations by Agents, form-letters, access to the file, introductory statements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates personalized information—agents explaining decisions, information sessions, clear form letters, access to one's own file, and chairmen's introductory statements to increase comprehension of procedure and decisions (Chapter 9, Section 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion and accuracy of application and initial data checks
rubrics_metrics.description: completion of the application, data check, opening of the file
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement that applications be properly completed and checked, and that a file be opened with accurate initial data to support correct decision-making (Chapter 1: preliminaries; Section 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of decision-making responsibilities and role clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: the distribution of responsibilities among agents and offices (Agents I and II, Headquarters, regional/district/local offices)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies clear lines of responsibility, roles of Agent I and Agent II, central units, and decentralized offices to ensure consistent, accountable decision-making (Chapter 2, Section 1–3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact with the claimant during decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: contact with the claimant: clarification of the application, job referral, encouragement to search for a job
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents should clarify unclear applications, actively refer claimants to jobs and encourage job search; such contacts are part of the substantive procedural duties of agents and are used to inform determinations (Chapter 2, Sections on contact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of decisions and implementation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: the decision: notification and implementation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions must be notified to claimants with reasons and implemented effectively; includes procedural steps for deliberation, notification and ensuring the decision takes effect (Chapter 2, Section 2C and 3D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit control: initiation, conduct, and reporting of investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: benefit control structure, initiation of investigations, conduct of investigations, investigation reporting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out standards for when and how investigations should start, how they should be conducted (evidence-gathering, fairness), and how investigation reports should be compiled and used in decisions (Chapter 3, Section 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of overpayments: discovery, notification, and UIC discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: determination of overpayments: discovery of overpayments, notification to the claimant, and the UIC's discretion in dealing with overpayments
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires clear procedures to detect overpayments, timely notification to affected claimants, application of discretion (e.g., whether to pursue recovery), and that decisions not to write off be appealable (Chapter 3, Section 2; Recommendation 61).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recovery mechanisms for overpayments: recoupment, tax reversal, collection
rubrics_metrics.description: recovery of overpayments through recoupment, tax reversal, collection measures (preliminary collection action, voluntary repayment agreements, locating debtors, garnishment, Federal Court action)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies a spectrum of recovery tools but recommends restricting harsher measures (garnishment, Federal Court registration) to cases where claimant is at fault and undue hardship will not be caused; tax reversal should require claimant consent with full understanding (Recommendations 63–64).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation periods and their character
rubrics_metrics.description: limitation periods set by sec. 49(4) be considered absolute and unalterable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation that statutory limitation periods be treated as absolute to provide legal certainty in recovery actions (Recommendation 60).

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing off overpayments and criteria for 'undue hardship'
rubrics_metrics.description: discretion to write off overpayments resulting from UIC error or omission and criteria for writing off on grounds of undue hardship
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes UIC discretion to write off overpayments caused by its errors unless claimant reasonably knew amounts were not due; recommends refining, publicizing and using 'financial insecurity' at time of violation as an extenuating circumstance; decisions not to write off should be appealable (Recommendations 61–62; Chapter 14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and delimitation of sanctions: administrative vs criminal
rubrics_metrics.description: delineation between administrative penalties and criminal sanctions, imposition and recovery of penalties
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Urges restriction of criminal sanctions to violations of the Act only (not Regulations), allowing due diligence defense, expansion of administrative penalties for regulatory violations (new sec. 47A), and considering financial insecurity as mitigating when choosing administrative rather than criminal sanctions (Recommendations 65–68).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to review and appeal formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: access to review: rights of appeal, appeal formalities, place of hearing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for broader and easier access to appeal tribunals, simplification of appeal formalities, clarity about hearing venues, and measures to make appeals accessible to claimants (Chapter 13, Section 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and independence of review tribunals
rubrics_metrics.description: organization of review tribunals: composition, reorganization of the higher tribunal (jurisdiction, structure, operation), autonomy of appeal tribunals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommends composition standards for Boards of referees, reorganization of higher tribunal (Umpire) for clearer jurisdiction/structure, and ensuring complete autonomy and higher profile for the second-level tribunal (Chapter 13, Section 2; proposals summarized in Part II).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and preparation for hearings before Boards and Umpire
rubrics_metrics.description: formation of the Board and preparations for the hearing; conduct of hearings; examination of appeals; decisions of Board of referees and the Umpire
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies pre-hearing preparation (making up the file, submissions), formation of panels, procedural control by higher tribunal over pre-hearing procedure, conduct norms during hearings, and standards for deliberation and issuing written decisions (Chapters 4–5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation and representation of claimants at hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: claimants' participation and its effects; types of claimant representation: unions, specialized organizations, legal aid
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures claimant participation (attendance, intervention) and success rates; recommends facilitating representation through unions, specialized organizations and legal aid; calls for UIC to accommodate representation (Chapter 7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Informing the decision-maker: documentation and fact-gathering standards
rubrics_metrics.description: gathering the facts and the documentation available to the decision-maker (Record of Employment, submissions, reports)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision-makers must have comprehensive, well-documented records: accurate Record of Employment, clear submissions, and reliable reports of prior proceedings. Emphasizes thoroughness and consistency in compiling the record for fair decisions (Chapter 10, Sections 1–2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criteria for factual determinations (internal yardsticks)
rubrics_metrics.description: assessing the facts: the problem of internal criteria (reasonable interval, medical yardsticks, labour market statistics)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates explicit use and disclosure of internal criteria (what counts as a reasonable interval of unemployment, standards for medical incapacity, appropriate labour market statistics) to increase predictability and fairness in discretionary assessments (Chapter 10, Section 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to be heard and opportunities for pre- and post-decision intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: participation prior to litigation: the right to be heard; opportunities for intervention before and after the decision
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures claimants have chances to present evidence and arguments both before decisions and in immediate post-decision stages, to address evidentiary issues and reduce litigation (Chapter 11, Section 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed in decision-making and organizational remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: speed in decision-making: organizational problems, computerization, integration of functions, and problems associated with time elements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies delay sources and recommends organizational changes (computerization, functional integration) to speed routine decision-making and reduce backlog, with special attention to litigation-related delays at Boards and Umpire (Chapter 12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of decisions: training and writing of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: the quality of decisions: training of members of Boards of referees and the writing of the decisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for enhanced training for tribunal members, clearer and better-reasoned written decisions, and standards for decision-writing to improve administrative justice and reduce need for judicial review (Chapter 13, Section 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication and prior warning about sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: prior warning to claimants of the existence of sanctions and complete information regarding the reasons for all decisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommends explicit communication to claimants about possible sanctions, and that all decisions include complete reasons so claimants understand basis and can exercise appeal rights; part of broader transparency objective (Part II proposals summarized).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on harsh recovery/enforcement measures
rubrics_metrics.description: restricting garnishment, Federal Court action and tax reversal to limited circumstances and requiring consent or evidence of fault
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes limiting garnishment and Federal Court registration to cases where claimant is at fault or convicted or has admitted awareness; tax reversal should require claimant consent with full understanding; restrict use to avoid undue hardship (Recommendations 63–64).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealability of administrative decisions about write-offs and recoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: decisions not to write off overpayments and other recovery decisions should be appealable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation that UIC decisions refusing write-offs or otherwise exercising recovery discretion be subject to appeal to ensure fairness and reviewability (Recommendation 61).
